bodyMarkdown:
## Using the Take Home Pay Calculator Australia

Whether you're negotiating a salary offer or checking your current hourly rate, our take home pay calculator australia gives you a clear picture of your annual earnings, fortnightly pay, and estimated tax. The tool works for permanent and casual employees, with a simple checkbox to add the 25% casual loading. You only need to enter your base hourly rate—never a rate that already includes casual loading.

### From Hourly to Annual: The Formula

The standard formula to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour. A permanent full-time employee on this rate would earn:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44 per year (before tax and super).

If you are a casual employee, you receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. The casual rate becomes $33.05 per hour. Using the same formula:

$33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80 per year (before tax and super).

Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter any hourly rate and instantly see the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. It also applies the casual loading if you select that option.

### Casual Loading Explained

Casual loading of 25% compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave, personal leave, and public holidays. It is paid on top of the base hourly rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the casual loading for award-covered employees, and the National Minimum Wage order includes it for award-free employees.

**Important:** When using the calculator, always enter your base hourly rate without casual loading. The checkbox adds the 25% automatically. If you already have a rate that already includes casual loading, you would be double-counting.

For more details, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the National Minimum Wage example, super on the permanent rate of $26.44 per hour is 12% of $52,245.44 = $6,269.33 per year. For casual employees, super is calculated on the casual rate including loading. So for the casual rate $33.05, super is 12% of $65,306.80 = $7,836.82 per year.

Our calculator shows super as an additional amount, not deducted from your pay. Your take-home pay is your gross annual salary minus tax and Medicare levy. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more.

### Tax and Medicare

The Australian Taxation Office's 2026–27 resident tax rates are:

- Nil up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this tool's update. This means your estimated tax may vary slightly.

For the National Minimum Wage permanent employee earning $52,245.44, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be approximately $5,647 (using the 2026–27 rates). The take-home pay would be around $46,598 per year. For the casual employee earning $65,306.80, estimated tax is about $9,592, leaving take-home pay of $55,715.

These are estimates only. Your actual tax may differ due to HELP, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

### Award Rates and the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. As of 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour for permanent employees. Many employees are covered by industry or occupation awards that set higher minimum rates. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for your correct rate.

The Fair Work Commission reviews the National Minimum Wage annually. Award rates are also adjusted. Our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page provides current figures.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026 show full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week. This is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for any specific job. Use [average pay](/topics/average-pay) for more context.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the National Minimum Wage permanent employee:

Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72
Fortnightly: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44

For casual: Weekly: $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
Fortnightly: $2,511.80

Our calculator shows both weekly and fortnightly amounts.

### How to Use the Calculator

Visit our [the timesheet](/) page. Enter your base hourly rate in the input field. If you are a casual employee, check the box labelled "Add 25% casual loading". The calculator will automatically update the annual, monthly, fortnightly, and weekly figures. It also shows the estimated tax, Medicare, and take-home pay. Super is displayed separately as an employer contribution.

You can adjust the hours per week if you work different hours. The default is 38 hours for full-time. Part-time workers can enter their usual hours.

The calculator is designed for quick estimates. For a binding pay calculation, refer to your award or agreement.

### Important Notes

This calculator provides an estimate based on the assumptions stated. It assumes the same hourly rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

For a more precise calculation, consult a tax professional or use the ATO's tax estimator.

Our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page has more details on after-tax pay.
